Sélène: French form of Selene, the Greek moon goddess, from selene, 'moon'.
Grâce: French for 'grace', from Latin gratia, 'favour, kindness'.
Wiktor: Polish form of Victor, from Latin victor, 'conqueror'.
Orhan: Turkish, probably 'great ruler' or 'chief'; the name of the second Ottoman sultan.
Adélie: French, from Adèle, Germanic adal, 'noble'. Also the name of a penguin and coast in Antarctica.
Zeger: Dutch and Flemish, from Germanic sigi 'victory' and ger 'spear': 'victorious spear'.
Martina: Latin feminine of Martinus, 'of Mars', the Roman god of war.
Léona: French feminine form of Léon, from Latin leo, 'lion'.
Fatou: West African form of Fatima, Arabic 'one who abstains' or 'captivating'.
João: Portuguese form of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'.
Zakarya: Arabic form of Zechariah, from Hebrew 'Yahweh remembers'.
León: Spanish form of Leo, from Latin leo, 'lion'.
Adama: Hebrew adamah, 'earth, soil'; also a West African given name (Fula and Mandinka) used for both sexes.
Dawoud: Arabic form of David, from Hebrew 'beloved'.
Valère: French form of Valerius, from Latin valere, 'to be strong, healthy'.
Sham: Arabic Sham, 'Syria' or 'Damascus' region, or Indian 'dark', short for Shyam. Origin depends on culture.
Maddy: English pet form of Madeleine, Madison or Madeline, ultimately from Magdala, the town of Mary Magdalene.
Bruna: Italian, Portuguese feminine of Bruno, from Germanic brun, 'brown'.
Tyago: Probably a variant of Thiago or Tiago, the Portuguese form of James, from Hebrew Yaakov.
Hanifa: Arabic, 'true believer, upright', feminine of Hanif.
Nias: Probably a short form of Elias or Tobias, or from the Indonesian island Nias; origin uncertain.
Lyvio: Probably a modern variant of Livio, Italian from Latin Livius, a Roman family name possibly 'bluish'.
Hussain: Arabic Husayn, diminutive of hasan, 'good, handsome'. Grandson of the Prophet Muhammad.
Usman: Turkish and South Asian form of Uthman, Arabic of uncertain meaning, perhaps 'baby bustard'.
Nate: English short form of Nathan or Nathaniel, from Hebrew 'he gave' or 'gift of God'.
Nayra: Arabic Nayra, 'bright, luminous'; also used in Spain, from Canary Islands usage.
Ezia: Probably a variant of Ezio or Ezra; origin uncertain, possibly Hebrew 'help'.
Linaya: Modern coined name, probably a blend of Lina and Maya or Amaya. Origin uncertain.
Leyth: Variant of Laith or Layth, Arabic 'lion'.
Jolien: Dutch, a blend of Jo and the -lien ending, or a form of Jolene; origin uncertain.
Claudia: Latin feminine of Claudius, a Roman family name from claudus, 'lame'.
Kyano: Modern coined name, perhaps from Greek kyanos, 'dark blue'. Origin uncertain.
Kiana: Possibly Hawaiian form of Diana, or Irish/Native American in origin; meaning uncertain.
Gijs: Dutch short form of Gijsbert, from Germanic gisil 'pledge' and berht 'bright'.
Roy: Scottish Gaelic ruadh, 'red'; or Old French roi, 'king'.
Nanou: French pet form of Anne, Hannah or Nathalie.
Lauranne: French blend of Laure and Anne; Laure from Latin laurus, 'laurel', Anne from Hebrew 'grace'.
Aiko: Japanese, commonly 'beloved child' or 'love child', depending on the characters.
Kate: Short form of Katherine, from Greek aikaterine, of uncertain meaning, later linked to katharos, 'pure'.
Lylou: French modern blend of Lily or Lyla and Lou. Origin as a coined name.
Jayson: Variant of Jason, Greek Iason, 'healer'. The leader of the Argonauts.
Remy: French, from Latin Remigius, 'oarsman'. Saint Remigius baptised Clovis.
Eugénie: French feminine form of Eugène, Greek Eugenios, 'well-born'.
Constantin: French and Romanian form of Constantine, from Latin constans, 'steadfast'.
Zina: Arabic Zina, 'beauty, adornment'; also a Slavic short form of Zinaida, 'of Zeus'.
Ester: Italian and Scandinavian form of Esther, perhaps Persian 'star' or Hebrew 'hidden'.
Mouad: Arabic Mu'adh, 'protected, sheltered'; a companion of the Prophet.
Oriana: Latin, 'golden' (from aurum), or possibly 'rising, dawn'. A literary name of Elizabeth I.
Dora: Short form of Dorothea or Theodora, Greek 'gift of God'; also simply Greek doron, 'gift'.
Jasmina: Form of Jasmine, from Persian yasmin, the flower name.
Rohan: Sanskrit, 'ascending'; also an Irish and Breton surname, and a place in Lord of the Rings.
Zacharie: French form of Zechariah, Hebrew Zekharyah, 'Yahweh remembers'.
Marylou: Combined form of Mary and Louise; Mary from Hebrew Miriam, Louise 'famous warrior'.
Wyatt: English, from a medieval name Wyot, from Old English wig 'war' and heard 'brave'.
Daniella: Feminine of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Asia: Name of the continent, probably from Akkadian asu, 'east, sunrise'; also a short form of Anastasia.
Nikola: Slavic form of Nicholas, Greek Nikolaos, 'victory of the people'.
Oliwia: Polish form of Olivia, from Latin oliva, 'olive tree'.
Loup: French for 'wolf'; a rare modern given name.
Ferdinand: Germanic, possibly 'bold journey' or 'peace-courage'; via Spanish Fernando.
Bilel: Arabic Bilal, 'moisture, water'; Bilal ibn Rabah was the first muezzin of Islam.
Markus: German and Scandinavian form of Mark, from Latin Marcus, probably 'of Mars'.
Mete: Turkish, from Mete Han, the Hun ruler (Modun); also Turkish mete 'hero'. Also Scandinavian 'mate'.
Mahaut: Old French form of Mathilde, Germanic 'mighty in battle'.
Helder: Portuguese, from Dutch or Germanic 'bright', or a form of Elder; origin uncertain. Also Dutch 'clear, bright'.
Marty: English pet form of Martin, Martha or Marta; Martin means 'of Mars'.
Malone: Irish surname, from Gaelic 'servant of Saint John', used as a modern given name.
Brianna: Feminine of Brian, Irish and Celtic, 'high, noble'.
Afnane: Arabic Afnan, 'branches', as in lush trees or many forms.
Sybille: French and German form of Sibyl, Greek sibylla, a female prophet.
Lizéa: Modern coined name, probably from Lizzie or Lise plus a vowel ending; origin uncertain.
Siloé: French form of Siloam, Hebrew 'sent', the pool in Jerusalem in the Bible.
Fenn: English, from Old English fenn, 'marsh, fen', a surname and modern given name.
Rian: Irish ri 'king' or Gaelic 'little king'; also Dutch short form of Marian or Adriaan.
Tomy: Variant of Tommy, a diminutive of Thomas, Aramaic 'twin'.
Cecile: French form of Cecilia, from Latin Caecilius, probably from caecus, 'blind'.
Massin: Probably a variant of Massine or Arabic Yassin; origin uncertain. Or from Mathis.
Ajla: Bosnian and Turkish, from Aylin or Arabic Ayla, 'halo around the moon' or 'oak tree'.
Efraim: Hebrew Efrayim, 'fruitful'. Son of Joseph in the Bible.
Altay: Turkish, from the Altai mountains, of uncertain origin, perhaps 'golden'.
Minthe: Greek Minthe, a nymph transformed into the mint plant; origin of the word is uncertain.
Laïa: Catalan, probably a short form of Eulàlia, Greek 'well-spoken'. Also a modern coined name.
Sef: Dutch and Flemish short form of Jozef, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Émilien: French form of Aemilianus, from the Roman family name Aemilius, probably 'rival'.
Aïna: Probably from Arabic ayna 'where' or Hawaiian/Japanese forms; origin uncertain. Or Catalan Aina, Anne.
Maïlo: Breton, probably from the saint name Malo or Maël, 'prince'. Origin uncertain.
Modest: From Latin modestus, 'moderate, modest'; a Slavic and Dutch usage via Saint Modestus.
Leyana: Modern coined name, probably a blend of Leila and Ana; origin uncertain.
Aylis: Modern coined name, perhaps a variant of Alice or Turkish Aylin; origin uncertain.
Rouguiatou: West African (Guinean) form of Ruqayyah, Arabic 'gentle, ascent', a daughter of the Prophet.
Bobbi: English pet form of Roberta or Barbara, used as an independent girls' name.
Niyah: Modern name, possibly from Swahili nia, 'purpose, intention' or Arabic niyyah 'intent'.
Efrem: Variant of Ephraim, Hebrew 'fruitful'; also Russian Yefrem.
Sébastien: French form of Sebastian, from Greek sebastos, 'venerable'.
Caroline: French feminine of Charles, from Germanic karl, 'free man'.
François: French form of Francis, from Latin Franciscus, 'Frenchman' or 'free man'.
Emeline: French form of Emmeline, from Germanic amal, 'work'.
Michaël: French and Dutch form of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Andy: English pet form of Andrew, from Greek andreios, 'manly'.
Sofiane: Arabic Sufyan, from a root meaning 'swift' or 'sails smoothly'.
Demi: English, from French demi, 'half', or short for Demetria, 'of Demeter'.
Yaro: Slavic short form of names like Jaroslav, 'fierce glory'; also Czech, Hausa and Japanese uses.
Berat: Turkish and Albanian, from Arabic bara'ah, 'innocence, acquittal'; also the Albanian city.
Alyssia: Variant of Alyssa, from Alice or Greek alysson, 'sane'; modern coined form.
Jaro: Czech and Slovak short form of Jaroslav, 'fierce' and 'glory'.
Asmae: Variant of Asma or Asmaa, Arabic 'loftier, more elevated, exalted'.
Vanina: Italian, probably from Giovanna, or a Corsican form of Vanna; ultimately Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Abdel: Arabic abd, 'servant', a prefix to a divine name such as Abdel-Rahman.
Ramazan: Turkish form of Ramadan, the Islamic month of fasting, from Arabic 'scorching heat'.
Robyn: English variant of Robin, from Robert, Germanic 'bright fame'; or the bird.
Mien: Dutch pet form of Wilhelmina or Mina; Wilhelmina means 'resolute protector'.
Allison: English, from a surname meaning 'son of Alice', Germanic 'noble kind'.
Enis: Turkish and Arabic Anis, 'friend, close companion'.
Maëly: Modern French coinage, probably from Maëlle or Maël (Breton 'prince').
Joe: English short form of Joseph, from Hebrew 'God will add'.
Isis: Egyptian goddess, Greek form of Aset, probably 'throne'.
Marley: English, from a surname meaning 'pleasant wood' or 'boundary wood'.
Peyton: English, from a surname and place name, 'Pega's estate'. Used for both sexes.
Giorgio: Italian form of George, Greek Georgios, 'farmer'.
Mayline: Modern French coined name, from May or Maïa and the -line ending. Origin uncertain.
Louan: Breton, possibly 'little fox' from Breton louarn, or a blend of Louis and Yoann. Origin uncertain.
Sibylle: French and German form of Sibyl, Greek sibylla, 'prophetess'.
Jozef: Dutch and Slavic form of Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Noelia: Spanish form of Noël, from Latin natalis, 'birthday', i.e. Christmas.
Sieg: Germanic sieg, 'victory'; a short form of names like Siegfried.
Mees: Dutch short form of Bartholomeus, Aramaic 'son of Talmai', or from Matthijs.
Mohamed-Ali: Arabic compound of Muhammad, 'praised', and Ali, 'high, exalted'.
Arielle: French feminine of Ariel, Hebrew 'lion of God'.
Nella: Short form of Antonella, Eleonora or Cornelia, or an independent pet form.
Deva: Sanskrit, 'divine, shining one', also a deity; also Welsh Deva, the Roman name for Chester.
Nessim: Arabic and Hebrew, from nasim, 'breeze', or nes 'miracle' in Hebrew; Sephardic given name.
Franciszek: Polish form of Francis, from Latin Franciscus, 'Frenchman'.
Ides: Probably a Dutch or Frisian form of Idesbald or Ide; origin uncertain. Possibly Old Norse 'woman'.
Issra: Arabic Isra, 'night journey' (of the Prophet Muhammad).
Jaak: Flemish and Estonian form of Jacob, Hebrew 'supplanter'.
Enaël: Modern Breton-style coinage, probably a blend of Enael and Maël; origin uncertain.
Asena: Turkish, from the mythical she-wolf of Turkic legend; origin uncertain, possibly Old Turkic 'noble wolf'.
Elisei: Romanian and Russian form of Elisha, from Hebrew 'God is salvation'.
Amedeo: Italian form of Amadeus, from Latin 'love God'.
Moris: Variant of Maurice, from Latin Mauritius, 'dark-skinned'; also a Sephardic Jewish form.
Noëlle: French feminine of Noël, from Latin natalis, 'birth', for Christmas.
Sekou: West African (Guinea, Mali) form of Shaykh, Arabic 'elder, learned man'.
Ilaf: Arabic, 'concord, harmony, familiarity'; possibly a variant of Ilaaf. Origin uncertain.
Leïa: Variant of Leia or Leah; Leah is Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'.
Yousuf: Arabic form of Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Priam: Greek Priamos, king of Troy; possibly 'redeemed' or 'bought back'. Origin uncertain.
Nobel: Swedish surname, possibly from Nöbbelöv; as a given name, likely from the Latin nobilis, 'noble'.
Ezéchiel: French form of Ezekiel, Hebrew Yechezkel, 'God strengthens'.
Sylia: Probably a variant of Sylvia, Latin 'forest'; or a Berber/Kabyle form of Silya. Origin uncertain.
Rae: English, short form of Rachel, or from Old English 'doe'; also a surname.
Ghazal: Arabic and Persian, a lyrical love poem; also 'gazelle' in some usage.
Nelio: Probably a short form of Cornelio or a variant of Nello, from Cornelius or Daniele; origin uncertain.
Thyam: Possibly a variant of Tiam or Thiam, a West African surname; origin uncertain.
Casian: Romanian form of Cassian, from Latin Cassianus, a Roman family name from Cassius, 'empty' or 'vain'.
Watin: Arabic Watan, 'homeland'; Watin is a modern spelling used for girls. Origin uncertain.
Cézan: Probably a variant of Cezanne, French surname from Cesana; as a given name, origin uncertain.
Amandine: French diminutive of Amanda, Latin 'worthy of love'.
Deborah: Hebrew Devorah, 'bee'. A biblical prophet and judge.
Tomas: Spanish, Czech and Lithuanian form of Thomas, Aramaic 'twin'.
Youri: Russian Yuri, form of George, Greek Georgios, 'farmer'.
Juan: Spanish form of John, Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'.
Yelena: Russian form of Helen, Greek 'torch' or 'shining one'.
Téa: Short form of Dorothea or Theodora, or from Greek thea, 'goddess'.
Tyméo: Modern French blend, probably of Timéo and Tyméo; origin uncertain, see Timeo.
Zachary: English form of Zechariah, Hebrew 'Yahweh remembers'.
Marouan: Variant of Marwan, Arabic of uncertain meaning, perhaps 'flint' or 'hard stone'.
Meryam: Arabic and Turkish form of Maryam, Mary, Hebrew Miriam, possibly 'beloved'.
Gina: Short form of Georgina, Regina or Luigina, thus 'farmer', 'queen' or 'famous warrior'.
Alicja: Polish form of Alice, Germanic Adalheidis, 'noble kind'.
Raffaele: Italian form of Raphael, Hebrew 'God heals'.
Délia: French form of Delia, from Delos, birthplace of Artemis; also a short form of Cordelia.
Stefania: Italian and Polish feminine of Stephen, from Greek stephanos, 'crown'.
Myra: Coined by 17th-century poet Fulke Greville; possibly from Greek myron 'perfume' or Latin mirari 'to admire'.
Yaniss: Variant of Yanis, a form of Ioannis or Jean, 'God is gracious'. Also Berber usage.
Giacomo: Italian form of Jacob or James, Hebrew 'supplanter'.
Torre: Italian and Spanish, 'tower'; also a Scandinavian variant of Thor. Origin depends on culture.
Wissam: Arabic, 'medal, badge of honour'; also 'handsome' in some use.
Elouise: Variant of Eloise or Héloïse, Germanic and possibly Louise, 'famous warrior'.
Elvis: Possibly from Irish Ailbhe, or Old Norse 'all-wise'; made famous by Elvis Presley. Origin uncertain.
Evie: English pet form of Eve or Evelyn; Eve is Hebrew 'life'.
